name: Apnea of Prematurity

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical diagnosis based on neonatal apnea episodes

criteria.description: Cessation of breathing lasting 20 seconds or longer, or shorter if accompanied by bradycardia or oxygen desaturation
Gestational age less than 37 weeks at birth
Exclusion of other causes of apnea such as infection, metabolic disturbances, or neurological disorders
Presence of bradycardia during apnea episodes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: At least one apnea episode in a premature infant with exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical; polysomnography may be used in complex cases

searchTerms: failure to gain weight as baby

laboratory: Normal metabolic panel unless secondary complications
Blood gas analysis may show hypoxemia and hypercapnia during episodes
imaging: Chest X-ray typically normal or shows prematurity-related lung changes
Brain ultrasound to exclude intracranial pathology if indicated
genetic: No specific genetic markers identified; multifactorial etiology
other: Polysomnography shows central apnea with associated bradycardia and oxygen desaturation

distinguishingFeatures: Chronic lung disease with persistent oxygen requirement
Apnea often accompanied by increased work of breathing
Apnea accompanied by temperature instability and lethargy
Apnea episodes temporally related to feeding

redFlags: Apnea episodes lasting longer than 20 seconds with severe bradycardia
Apnea associated with seizures or altered consciousness
Failure to respond to standard supportive care and methylxanthine therapy
references: Martin RJ, et al. Apnea of prematurity: pathophysiology and management. Pediatr Pulmonol. 2019.
American Academy of Pediatrics Clinical Report on Apnea of Prematurity, 2020
